 Facilities Brewers fans bought more than 30,000 ‘Racing Sausages’ in first two World Series games
 By Mike Mazzeo 10.26.2026 Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} In Games 1-2 of the World Series, fans bought more than 300,000 F&B items (nearly four items per person), according to data from provider Delaware North. Getty Images MILWAUKEE – Brewers fans haven’t just been buying World Series tickets and merchandise. They’ve also been hitting the concession stands in droves to purchase food and beverage. In Games 1-2 of the Fall Classic at American Family Field, fans bought more than 300,000 F&B items (nearly four items per person), according to data from provider Delaware North. 
 That included more than 30,000 Racing Sausages (Polish, Italian, hot dog and brat). While they seesaw during the season, brats (11,000) beat hot dogs (10,000) as the WS top seller. Fans also purchased more than 7,000 orders of peanuts, 3,500 pretzels and 3,000 cheese curds. Delaware North also sold approximately 3,000 specialty items, which are created for the postseason, including the Brat Rangoon, Walk-Off Burger, Monkey Bread, Thai Elote Dog, Pasty and Prime Rib. Additionally, Delaware North did 4x its souvenir numbers (including koozies, cups and different baseball bats) than in the NLCS. 
 “It takes a Delaware North army,” said Kevin Jezewski , GM/Delaware North Sportservice at Am Fam Field. “It’s not just a local event. It’s a worldwide event. We have people coming from all over the world to try our food, and for us it’s important that Milwaukee’s food scene is shown well throughout this ballpark.” 
 While the postseason participants aren’t known until the end of the regular season, Delaware North says the planning process begins about three months out in terms of recipe development, staffing and scheduling, while also ensuring that they have enough beer and sausages via suppliers Molson-Coors and Johnsonville. 
 As far as the World Series is concerned, Delaware North has 800 to 1,000 staffers for games, though prep among a few hundred staffers (including culinary, bartenders, support staff etc. …) begins a few days earlier. Additionally, 40 staffers were flown in to help from organizations like Packers, Texas Rangers and Braves. Delaware North counts 10 MLB teams as clients: the Tigers (1930), Reds (1939), White Sox (1940), Cardinals (1953), Brewers (1970), Guardians (1994), Rangers (1994), Padres (2004), Twins (2010) and Braves (2016). After the World Series ends, though, it is unclear how next year will work given baseball’s uncertainty on the labor front. 
 “That’s for tomorrow,” said Tom Barney , President/Delaware North Sportservice. “We can only jump the hurdles in order. Today, we’re celebrating with the Brewers and the Rays. After a championship is crowned, we’ll move onto the next (order of business).”
